rules.problem: Structure (sudden face/tongue swelling AND any of) and 'possible' for 'check for anaphylaxis' are right; BP<90/60 as SBP<90 OR DBP<60 acceptable. Allergen exposure has no time window, so any medication exposure or old insect bite plus sudden face swelling qualifies.
Faithful AND of painful red facial swelling and T>=38; only the Facial swelling concept choice.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable orbital cellulitis from facial cellulitis
rules.problem: Re-expands facial cellulitis criteria correctly, but drops 'whole' eyelid, so any eyelid swelling with facial cellulitis yields probable orbital cellulitis.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable kidney disease from facial swelling
Diagnose probable post-herpetic neuralgia of face
rules.problem: History of herpes zoster anywhere satisfies 'previous shingles on same side of face'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable sinusitis from face pain
rules.problem: Requires all five features in AND (pain, tenderness, headache, thick discharge, recent cold), stricter than the descriptive box may intend; positional headache qualifier dropped.
Sudden unilateral facial weakness AND (forehead involved OR unable to close eye) matches the page and is consistent with the stroke rule's forehead-sparing split.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable angioedema from face swelling
Diagnose probable mumps from painful face swelling
rules.problem: AND of fever, headache and body pain follows 'with fever, headache, body pain' literally; Facial swelling concept choice.

rules.rule: Urgent: face symptoms with stroke, anaphylaxis, facial cellulitis or kidney disease signs
rules.problem: Urgent matches the red-box heading. But the outer face-symptom anchor omits tongue swelling, so sudden tongue swelling with difficulty breathing is not escalated unless a face symptom is also recorded; non-sudden speech/visual items escalate; active_condition Kidney disease escalates any face symptom in a known CKD patient.

summary: Most consequential: the Urgent priority evaluation and the urgent check_for task are anchored on a face-symptom OR that leaves out tongue swelling, so 'Sudden face/tongue swelling' with breathing difficulty only escalates if a face finding is also recorded; in the same rule, difficulty speaking and visual disturbance count without the page's 'new sudden' qualifier. Allergen exposure loses the footnote's 'within the past few hours' window, orbital cellulitis drops 'whole' eyelid, and face/tongue swelling are postcoordinated where precoordinated Facial swelling / Tongue swelling exist. No invented or wrong conditions found.
